create.name: Bruce Tift
create.bio:
Bruce Tift is a Boulder-based teacher and author who has spent more than four decades practising Vajrayana Buddhism. He was a student of Chögyam Trungpa Rinpoche, holds a master's degree in psychology, and for twenty-five years taught at Naropa University in Boulder, Colorado, the town where he lives. He trained and worked as a marriage and family therapist, and his writing explores how Buddhist practice and Western psychology can sit side by side.

His book Already Free, published by Sounds True, compares two ways of approaching freedom from suffering: the developmental approach, which looks at how early experience shapes us, and what he calls the fruitional approach of Buddhism, which starts from the view that freedom is available in each moment rather than being a distant goal. He now offers occasional one-to-one consultations by phone or video for people wanting support with personal growth, drawing on awareness practice and gently questioning the habits and stories we identify with. His blog essays set out a basic Buddhist view of experience, and he has spoken about his work on podcasts including Sounds True's Insights at the Edge and Lion's Roar.

books.title: Already Free: Buddhism Meets Psychotherapy on the Path of Liberation
books.author: Bruce Tift
books.description: A book that sets the Western developmental view of the self beside the Buddhist view that freedom is already present, and asks how each can inform the other in daily life, relationships and practice.

courses.title: One-to-one consultation
courses.description: Sixty-minute sessions by phone or video, no more often than once every four weeks, for people seeking support with personal growth. He draws on decades of Vajrayana practice and offers practices that loosen identification with old patterns.
